gloss: it goes without saying; needless to say

definitions.gloss: it goes without saying; needless to say; obviously
definitions.explanation: An adverbial expression used to introduce something the speaker considers self-evident or universally understood. Literally 'without even needing to say it.'

examples.japanese: {言|い}うまでもなく{大切|たいせつ}なことだ。
examples.english: It goes without saying that this is important.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}が{大事|だいじ}なのは{言|い}うまでもない。
examples.english: Needless to say, health is important.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{実力|じつりょく}は{言|い}うまでもなく、{人柄|ひとがら}もすばらしい。
examples.english: His ability goes without saying, and his character is also wonderful.

notes:
Literally 'without it reaching the point of saying' — composed of {言|い}う (to say) + まで (until) + も (even) + なく (without). Expresses that something is so obvious it does not need to be stated.

FORMS:
- {言|い}うまでもなく — adverbial form, used mid-sentence
- {言|い}うまでもない — predicate form, used at the end of a clause
- {言|い}うまでもないことだが — 'this is obvious, but...' (used to preface something)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {言|い}うまでもなく、〜 — Needless to say, ...
- 〜は{言|い}うまでもない — ... goes without saying
- 〜は{言|い}うまでもなく、〜も — not only ..., but also ...

SIMILAR WORDS:
- もちろん — of course; less formal, used in everyday speech
- むろん — of course; literary variant of もちろん
- {当然|とうぜん} — naturally; focuses on logical expectation rather than rhetorical emphasis

REGISTER:
Somewhat formal. Common in writing, speeches, and structured arguments. In casual speech, もちろん is more natural.
